headline: the two enumeration methods agree on kinds, axioms and module coverage; the probe inventory contains 12,364 distinct names vs 12,361 in the grouped audit table

cause.class: generated declarations and whole-environment module attribution
cause.detail: all discrepant names are compiler/attribute-generated lemmas of the shape `*.eq_1`, `*.congr_simp` (not written literally in any release source). A probe imports one module, so `Environment.getModuleIdxFor?` (const2ModIdx, first-wins via insertIfNew) attributes each generated name to the module being probed. In a whole-partition environment the same name is registered first by whichever imported module generates it first -- in three cases a non-target module -- so the grouped audit's target-module filter drops it or attributes it to a different target module. Deduplication in declarations.tsv keeps one row per name.
cause.not_a_soundness_issue: the missing names are generated lemmas whose cones were checked separately: baseline/audit/depcheck/MissedDeclConeCheck.lean exits 0, verbatim results below

semantics: the v1 table's single-module attribution and 12,361-name count remain correct as a deduplicated enumeration; the package declaration set is 12,364 distinct names once generated declarations found only by per-module probing are included, and all are within the approved cone set
